audit.whatIsWrong: Olaf held five of seven chart rows on a 50.27% Emerald+ win rate over 750 games — a dead-even matchup drawn as a losing one — and two of those rows contradicted the text beside them. whys[4] says the level-6 all-in math 'is genuinely even' while the chart gave Level 6 to Olaf, and whys[6] says 'your proxy-poison engine is fully online' with the late paragraph saying 'in the 1v1 split-push context you own this stage' while the chart gave 2+ items to Olaf.
audit.why: The packet chart (Olaf, Olaf, Olaf, Skill, Skill, Skill, Singed) matches the prose and matches a 50.27% split.
audit.corrected: Level 6 to Skill and 2+ items to Singed, flipped as one atomic group across both layers, with those two phase whys rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff says EVEN but diffRating says 8.5/10 and the final-rating row says 'Hard matchup' — the page contradicts itself on a 50.27% matchup. Phase whys were template text naming no Olaf ability or number.
audit.why: An even win rate with a losing early game reads around 6/10, not 8.5.
audit.corrected: diffRating 6/10, difficulty and final-rating rows brought in line with the EVEN label; phase whys now name Undertow (9s, 1000 range), Reckless Swing (11s), Tough It Out (16s) and Ragnarok (100s).

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's account of Ragnarok is incomplete in the way that decides the lane. Riot: 'He passively gains increased armor and magic resist. He can activate this ability to become immune to disables FOR AS LONG AS HE KEEPS ATTACKING.' The page says only that it makes him CC-immune and that he 'walks straight through your glue pool', and tells the reader to bait it out. The real counter is the opposite of baiting: a Singed who breaks off and gives Olaf nothing to swing at lets the immunity lapse on its own. The armour and MR are also permanent from level 6, not part of the active — that changes when you can commit. Second, Undertow's cooldown is treated as a window: 'his Undertow cooldown creates gaps you can exploit'. Riot: 'If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset' — the 9 seconds only apply if he does not walk over it, so the play is to pull him away from the axe, not to count. Undertow also reduces ARMOUR, which the page never mentions.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon descriptions for Olaf Q and R.
audit.corrected: Ragnarok re-described as passive resists plus an attack-gated immunity you outlast by denying a target; Undertow's pickup reset and armour shred written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Vicious Strikes' is credited with Olaf's lifesteal in three places (early, whys[2], late). There is no ability called Vicious Strikes in Olaf's kit — his W is Tough It Out, which grants attack speed and a SHIELD and no healing at all. The lifesteal is on his passive, Berserker Rage, and it scales with MISSING health, so he heals harder the lower he gets. Getting that wrong inverts the advice: the page implies chipping him down weakens his sustain when it strengthens it.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon: Berserker Rage — 'Olaf gains Attack Speed and Life Steal based on his missing Health'; Tough It Out — 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield.'
audit.corrected: Lifesteal re-attributed to Berserker Rage with the missing-health scaling stated; Tough It Out named as the shield that eats your commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere on either layer.
audit.why: Undertow 9 flat at 1000 range but reset on pickup; Tough It Out 16/15/14/13/12; Reckless Swing 11/10/9/8/7 at 325 range, and it costs Olaf health, refunded only if it kills; Ragnarok 100/90/80.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into the phase whys, spikes, cooldown block, dos/donts and the interactions row.

edits.before: Levels one through three are Olaf's lane. His Undertow axe slows you on approach, Reckless Swing deals true damage that ignores your armor, and Vicious Strikes gives him lifesteal sustain that lets him win the attrition trade you would normally run. Do not try to run past him the way you would a Nasus or Malphite — he will stick to you with the slow and cash Reckless Swing before your Poison Trail accumulates enough damage to matter. Proxy behind his wave instead: absorb the caster minions under his tower, force him to choose between the wave and chasing you, and avoid any direct duel until you have items to support it.
edits.after: Levels one through three are Olaf's lane. His Undertow axe slows you on approach, Reckless Swing deals true damage that ignores your armor, and Berserker Rage's lifesteal grows as his health drops, so the attrition trade you would normally win goes to him. Do not try to run past him the way you would a Nasus or Malphite — he will stick to you with the slow and cash Reckless Swing before your Poison Trail accumulates enough damage to matter. Proxy behind his wave instead: absorb the caster minions under his tower, force him to choose between the wave and chasing you, and avoid any direct duel until you have items to support it.

edits.before: Levels four through six are where the lane balances out. You can begin running your proxy-poison pattern more aggressively as his ability to stick to you depends on landing Undertow, which has a travel time you can juke by changing direction. The critical variable at level six is Ragnarok — when he activates it, your Mega Adhesive root stops working entirely and he walks straight through your glue pool. Never use your Fling-glue combo as an opener into his R; instead, bait him to burn Ragnarok in a chase, then turn on him once it expires and he is rooted-able again. Insanity Potion gives you enough armor, MR, and movement speed that a post-Ragnarok all-in can actually favor you.
edits.after: Levels four through six are where the lane balances out. The critical variable at level six is Ragnarok — the disable immunity only lasts while he keeps attacking, so break off and it expires on its own. Never use your Fling-glue combo as an opener into his R; instead, make him chase with nothing to swing at, then turn once Ragnarok lapses and the goo roots him again. Insanity Potion gives you enough armor, MR, and movement speed that a post-Ragnarok all-in can actually favor you.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter changes the entire equation: Poison Trail now applies a permanent slow to Olaf every tick, meaning he can no longer freely walk through your cloud between Reckless Swing hits without taking mounting attrition. At two items your side-lane proxy pattern becomes nearly impossible for him to stop — chasing you down a poisoned corridor eats his health faster than his Vicious Strikes lifesteal can recover, and a well-timed Fling into a Mega Adhesive pool ends any overcommit cleanly. Respect his team-fight R window but in the 1v1 split-push context you own this stage — he cannot duel you without taking poison attrition, and he cannot disengage once you stick the glue.

notes: 'Vicious Strikes' is not an Olaf ability — this is the same class of error as the calibration examples. His W is Tough It Out (attack speed plus a SHIELD, no healing); the lifesteal is on the passive Berserker Rage and it scales with MISSING health, which reverses the page's implied advice about chipping him down. The other big one: Ragnarok's disable immunity lasts only 'for as long as he keeps attacking', so the counter is to give him nothing to swing at rather than to bait the ult, and its armour/MR are a permanent passive from 6 rather than part of the active. Undertow's cooldown is 9s but resets whenever he walks over the thrown axe, so the page's 'exploit his Undertow cooldown' advice needed replacing with denying the pickup. Undertow's derived 'grounding' flag is a false positive (Riot text: reduces Armor and Move Speed only) and was not written. Chart flipped in two rows to the packet; diff/diffRating/final-rating were self-contradictory (EVEN vs 8.5/10 vs 'Hard matchup') and are now consistent at 6/10.
